Expects logarithmized data, except when flavor='seurat_v3' in which count data is expected.

Depending on flavor, this reproduces the R-implementations of Seurat [Satija15], Cell Ranger [Zheng17], and Seurat v3 [Stuart19].

For the dispersion-based methods ([Satija15] and [Zheng17]), the normalized dispersion is obtained by scaling with the mean and standard deviation of the dispersions for features falling into a given bin for mean expression of features. This means that for each bin of mean expression, highly variable features are selected.

For [Stuart19], a normalized variance for each feature is computed. First, the data are standardized (i.e., z-score normalization per feature) with a regularized standard deviation. Next, the normalized variance is computed as the variance of each feature after the transformation. Features are ranked by the normalized variance.

`--flavor`
:::

::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"seurat"`

:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_top_features`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of highly-variable features to keep. Mandatory if flavor='seurat_v3'.

::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--min_mean`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If n_top_features is defined, this and all other cutoffs for the means and the normalized dispersions are ignored. Ignored if flavor='seurat_v3'.

::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.0125`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_mean`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If n_top_features is defined, this and all other cutoffs for the means and the normalized dispersions are ignored. Ignored if flavor='seurat_v3'.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `3.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--min_disp`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If n_top_features is defined, this and all other cutoffs for the means and the normalized dispersions are ignored. Ignored if flavor='seurat_v3'.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.5`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_disp`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If n_top_features is defined, this and all other cutoffs for the means and the normalized dispersions are ignored. Ignored if flavor='seurat_v3'. Default is +inf.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--span`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The fraction of the data (cells) used when estimating the variance in the loess model fit if flavor='seurat_v3'.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.3`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_bins`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of bins for binning the mean feature expression. Normalization is done with respect to each bin. If just a single feature falls into a bin, the normalized dispersion is artificially set to 1.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `20`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--obs_batch_key`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
If specified, highly-variable features are selected within each batch separately and merged. This simple
process avoids the selection of batch-specific features and acts as a lightweight batch correction method.
For all flavors, features are first sorted by how many batches they are a HVG. For dispersion-based flavors
ties are broken by normalized dispersion. If flavor = 'seurat_v3', ties are broken by the median (across
batches) rank based on within-batch normalized variance.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--output_compression`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Compression format to use for the output AnnData and/or Mudata H5 files.
By default no compression is applied.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"gzip"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"gzip"`, `"lzf"`
:::
::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/feature_annotation/highly_variable_features_scanpy/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/feature_annotation/highly_variable_features_scanpy);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/feature_annotation/highly_variable_features_scanpy/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
